checkedCadence: Weekly source check; urgent changes can be added through the Signal Intel Desk daily task.
method: Sourced, dated estimates only. No fake live counters. Red counters show figures or estimate markers only; titles and explanations render underneath. Where a reliable single estimate is not available, the counter uses an estimate-status value such as EST. SOURCE-SPLIT, MIN. REPORTED, EST. UNDERCOUNT, or STATUS-SPLIT. Crime, sexual assault, trafficking, migrant-status, nationality, ethnicity, suspect, charge, conviction, victim, and report categories must not be merged. This file was checked on 2026-08-17 against official or high-reliability lanes; unchanged live figures mean no stronger sourced replacement was found during the check.

panels.title: Gaza / Israel War
panels.status: Gaza Health Ministry reported death-toll lane; combatant/civilian split contested
panels.description: Checked 2026-08-17. No stronger official replacement cumulative total was found during this weekly check, so the Gaza Health Ministry reported death-toll lane remains above 73,000 since 2023-10-07. OCHA's latest indexed Gaza humanitarian situation report remains the 2026-07-23 report, which separately recorded 1,180 reported fatalities and 3,810 injuries since the ceasefire announcement of 2025-10-10. These are reported ministry counts, not independently verified combatant/civilian classifications. Keep Gaza deaths, Israeli deaths, hostages, injuries, child deaths, famine indicators, disputed official claims, and ceasefire-period casualties separate.
panels.sourceLabel: Gaza Health Ministry / OCHA OPT situation report 2026-07-23 / OHCHR / UN Commission / Reuters / AP

panels.title: Ukraine War
panels.status: OHCHR verified civilian baseline; real toll likely higher
panels.description: Checked 2026-08-17. OHCHR's latest indexed cumulative verified baseline, published 2026-07-14, is at least 16,431 civilians killed, including 803 children, and 48,613 injured, including 2,960 children, since 2022-02-24. The same June 2026 update verified at least 293 civilians killed and 1,990 injured in June, the highest combined monthly civilian-casualty level since April 2022. In the first six months of 2026, OHCHR verified 1,396 killed and 7,978 injured, 37% above the same period in 2025. Keep verified civilian deaths, injuries, military casualties, missing persons, displacement, occupied-territory reporting limits, Russian-reported but UN-unverified figures, and infrastructure attacks separate.
panels.sourceLabel: OHCHR Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine update 2026-07-14 / UNHCR / OCHA

panels.title: Sudan / Darfur
panels.status: Minimum reported death lane; wider death estimates, displacement, famine, and health collapse separate
panels.description: Checked 2026-08-17. No stronger nationwide confirmed death total replaced the minimum reported lane. WHO reported on 2026-04-14 that 34 million people needed aid and 21 million lacked health services. Keep verified killings, mass-casualty reports, higher disputed estimates, displacement categories, famine, hospital attacks, siege conditions, cholera, deportations, returns and humanitarian access collapse separate.
panels.sourceLabel: UNHCR Sudan Situation dashboard updated 2026-07-20 / WHO 2026-04-14 / OHCHR / OCHA / IPC / IOM / WFP / UNICEF / AP / Reuters

panels.title: Migration / Irregular Immigration
panels.status: Country and route data only; no honest global illegal-immigration counter
panels.description: Checked 2026-08-17. No reliable single global irregular-migration counter exists. UK Home Office official statistics updated 2026-07-16 recorded 43,806 detected arrivals via illegal routes in the year ending March 2026, including 39,271 small-boat arrivals; the Home Office cautions that detections do not capture all arrivals and can include repeat detections. The same release recorded 39,007 returns from the UK in the year ending March 2026, including enforced and voluntary returns, plus 17,623 people refused entry on arrival who subsequently departed. Eurostat reported 42,960 first-time EU asylum applicants in April 2026 and 9,145 subsequent applicants; in Q1 2026, 108,475 non-EU citizens were ordered to leave an EU country and 34,550 were returned to third countries following an order to leave. IOM DTM recorded 51,259 arrivals to Europe through 2026-07-27; this route-monitoring total is not a count of all unauthorized migration. The next UK year-ending-June release is scheduled for 2026-08-27, so no later quarterly UK baseline was substituted during this check. Keep detections, persons, repeat crossings, asylum applications, subsequent applications, temporary protection, regularisation applications, returns, removals, refusals and departures, estimated unauthorized populations, and missing migrants separate.
panels.sourceLabel: UK Home Office Immigration system statistics updated 2026-07-16 / Eurostat asylum update 2026-07-16 / Eurostat returns 2026-06-30 / IOM DTM Europe arrivals through 2026-07-27 / Frontex / CBP / official national agencies

The Europe figure is a provisional regional route-monitoring total and must not be added to or substituted for the global 2025 baseline. panels.sourceLabel: IOM Missing Migrants / IOM DTM Europe arrivals through 2026-07-27 / Reuters

panels.title: Trafficking / Sexual Exploitation
panels.status: UNODC 2024 detected-victims lane; child-share included
panels.description: Checked 2026-08-17. UNODC's 2024 Global Report remains the latest comparable global detected-victim lane: 69,627 detected trafficking victims in 2022 and children at 38% of detected victims. Separately, Europol reported on 2026-07-06 that Operation GLOBAL CHAIN, conducted across 59 countries from 8 to 12 June 2026, identified 2,070 victims and potential victims, including 162 minors, and produced 1,024 arrests, 334 for suspected human trafficking; 465 new investigations were opened. Europol reported 64.2% of identified victims/potential victims were trafficked for sexual exploitation, rising to 86.4% among the identified minors. This is an operational snapshot, not a prevalence estimate. Keep detected victims, potential victims, estimated victims, exploitation type, arrests, convictions, forced labour, sexual exploitation, child share, and profit estimates separate.
panels.sourceLabel: UNODC Global Report 2024 / Europol-Frontex-INTERPOL Operation GLOBAL CHAIN published 2026-07-06 / ILO

panels.title: Vaccines: Damages & Compensation
panels.status: VICP compensation baseline plus CICP alleged, pending, eligible, compensated and denied lanes separated
panels.description: Checked 2026-08-17. HRSA's latest CICP aggregate remains dated 2026-07-01: 14,146 COVID-19 claims filed, 6,562 pending or in review, 7,584 decisions, 112 found eligible, 62 compensated, 46 pending benefits determination, 4 with no eligible reported expenses, and 7,472 denied. Across all covered countermeasures, CICP reported 14,755 claims ever filed, 152 found eligible and 92 compensated; HRSA's compensated-claims table totals $13,618,257.12 paid across those 92 CICP claims. Of the COVID-19 claims, 11,055 alleged vaccine injury or death; alleged claims are not causal findings, and HRSA states temporal association alone does not establish causation. For VICP, the Congressional Research Service reports more than $5.3 billion paid in compensation from program implementation through 2025-02-01, with 28,292 petitions filed, 24,602 adjudicated and 11,659 determined to merit compensation. HRSA's VICP data page was updated 2026-07-01 and notes that about 60% of compensation awards result from negotiated settlements in which HHS did not conclude that the vaccine caused the alleged injury. Adverse-event reports, alleged claims, compensated claims, pending claims, rejected claims, causal findings, litigation claims, and scheme applications must remain separate.
panels.sourceLabel: HRSA CICP aggregate and compensated-claims data as of 2026-07-01 / HRSA VICP data updated 2026-07-01 / U.S. Congressional Research Service VICP cumulative baseline through 2025-02-01 / UK VDPS

panels.title: Medical / System Failure
panels.status: Sudan facilities/services at risk and potentially affected population; other theaters separate
panels.description: Checked 2026-08-17. No single honest global medical-collapse counter exists. The WHO-led Sudan Health Cluster warned on 2026-06-17 that a funding disruption placed 335 health facilities and services across 13 states at risk, potentially affecting about 3.35 million people and 1,848 health workers. WHO separately reported on 2026-04-14 that 37% of health facilities across Sudan's 18 states were non-functional, 21 million people lacked health services, and WHO had verified 217 attacks on health care since 2023-04-15, causing 2,052 deaths and 810 injuries. In Gaza, OCHA reported on 2026-07-16 that only 44% of health service points mapped before October 2023 were functioning. These are theater-specific service-capacity and verified-attack indicators, not a global death total. Keep hospital attacks, facility functionality, medicine shortages, blocked aid, disease outbreaks, healthcare-worker deaths, excess mortality, patient backlogs, and service collapse separate.
panels.sourceLabel: WHO Sudan Health Cluster 2026-06-17 / WHO Sudan update 2026-04-14 / OCHA OPT situation report 2026-07-16 / WHO HeRAMS
